fixes.explanation: That's right, friend. These disciples tell Paul, “we have not even heard that there is a Holy Spirit.” (Acts 19:2) Paul asks one short question and gets that answer. I think he had more to say after that, and he did.

Close, friend, but the text goes further than that. These disciples tell Paul, “we have not even heard that there is a Holy Spirit.” (Acts 19:2) They haven't heard of Him at all, which is a lot more than not knowing Him well. Then Paul asks, “Into what, then, were you baptized?” (Acts 19:3)

Yes, friend. They answer Paul, “The baptism of John…” (Acts 19:3) Paul then says John's baptism was a baptism of repentance (Acts 19:4). I think that answer tells Paul right where to pick up the conversation.

Moses is a big name, but he doesn't come up in this scene. When Paul asks into what they were baptized, the disciples answer, “The baptism of John…” (Acts 19:3) Paul then explains that John's baptism was a baptism of repentance (Acts 19:4). Stick with the answer they actually give.
That's the one, friend. Paul says John “…told the people to believe in the One coming after him, that is, in Jesus.” (Acts 19:4) Paul names Him plainly, so nobody has to guess.

Elijah is a big name, but Paul doesn't name him here. He says John told people to believe in the One coming after him, “…that is, in Jesus.” (Acts 19:4) The text gives the name outright, so there's nothing to guess. You can set Elijah back on the shelf for this one.

Apollos only comes up at the start of the passage, and he's at Corinth when Paul reaches Ephesus (Acts 19:1). The One John pointed to is the One Paul names: “…that is, in Jesus.” (Acts 19:4) Apollos didn't need the job. Friend, I've been mixed up with the spatula before, so no shame.
Yes, friend. “On hearing this, they were baptized into the name of the Lord Jesus.” (Acts 19:5) Paul explains, and they listen. Then they are baptized.
No flash of light shows up in this scene, friend. The text says, “…the Holy Spirit came upon them, and they spoke in tongues and prophesied.” (Acts 19:6) Nobody is described falling down.

Not this time, friend. After the three months, “…some of them stubbornly refused to believe and publicly maligned the Way…” (Acts 19:9) So not every single person believed. Paul still spoke boldly for those three months.

Water from the pool of Siloam doesn't come up in this scene, friend. Here the text says, “…even handkerchiefs and aprons that had touched him were taken to the sick…” (Acts 19:12) It's cloth that gets carried.
That's the name, friend. The exorcists said, “I command you by Jesus, whom Paul proclaims.” (Acts 19:13) They pointed to Paul's preaching as their line. I think that's about to cause trouble.
Peter doesn't get named in these exorcists' line, friend. They said, “I command you by Jesus, whom Paul proclaims.” (Acts 19:13) Paul is the one they point to. Peter isn't part of this line.

That's exactly what it says, friend. “Jesus I know, and I know about Paul, but who are you?” (Acts 19:15) The sons of Sceva, a Jewish chief priest, get a question aimed right at them. It's a question nobody wants to get at work, let alone from that.

The spirit never asks for Paul, friend. What it says is, “Jesus I know, and I know about Paul, but who are you?” (Acts 19:15) It mentions Paul, then turns to the sons of Sceva, a Jewish chief priest's sons, with a question.

It's the other way around, friend. The spirit says, “Jesus I know, and I know about Paul, but who are you?” (Acts 19:15) It says it knows Jesus. Then it asks who the sons of Sceva, a Jewish chief priest's sons, are.
That's what the text says, friend. “The attack was so violent that they ran out of the house naked and wounded.” (Acts 19:16) This is a heavy part, and I think this one hurts.

Yes, friend. “Many who had believed now came forward, confessing and disclosing their deeds.” (Acts 19:18) They came forward and disclosed their deeds. That takes guts, and I'd rather confess a burnt batch.

That's right, friend. “…a number of those who had practiced magic arts brought their books and burned them in front of everyone.” (Acts 19:19) When the value of those books was calculated, it came to fifty thousand drachmas. And they still lit the match in front of everyone.
No shovels in this scene, friend. The text says they “…brought their books and burned them in front of everyone.” (Acts 19:19) They burned them, and they did it in front of everyone.

Yes, friend. “So the word of the Lord powerfully continued to spread and prevail.” (Acts 19:20) After the fear, the confessions and the burning books, the word kept on spreading. That's how this passage ends.
